summary: @testsecuiitytestme/cache-helper ships a native-addon dropper that stages and executes an opaque payload
details: The package advertises itself as a `Cache helper utilities` library but its only runtime effect is to load a prebuilt native addon via `require('node-gyp-build')(__dirname)` from `index.js`, with `node-gyp-build` also declared as the `install` script so the addon is resolved on `npm install` and again on every `require` of the package. The tarball ships prebuilt addons for `linux-x64` and `win32-x64` alongside a 2.4 MB opaque `.napi_cache` blob whose bytes are identical across platforms and do not correspond to any shipped source. The Linux ELF contains strings `%s/.napi_cache`, `/tmp/.%u`, `../addon.c`, and `addon.node`, and imports `fork`, `setsid`, `execlp`, `chmod`, `fopen64`, `fwrite`, `getenv`, `_exit` — the shape of code that writes the sibling blob to a staging path, makes it executable, and spawns it as a detached child process. The same ELF embeds explicit anti-analysis checks: environment-variable probes for CI providers (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `CIRCLECI`, `JENKINS_URL`, `BUILDKITE`, `CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID`, `APPVEYOR`, `SEMAPHORE`, `TEAMCITY_VERSION`, `BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER`, `NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT`, `CF_BUILD_ID`, `SCREWDRIVER`), container indicators (`/proc/1/cgroup`, `containerd`, `/proc/1/cmdline`, `dockerinit`), and debugger detection (`/proc/self/status` with `TracerPid:`, `/proc/self/maps`) — behaviors with no relationship to a cache utility and consistent with sandbox evasion around dropper execution. The scope name `@testsecuiitytestme` is a misspelling of `security` and, together with the brand/contents mismatch (claimed utility vs. shipped native dropper), is consistent with a disposable delivery vehicle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
